translations.answer: The thread explanation states that dummy simulation and MPC use the same model, and the zero-velocity contact constraint is used to maintain contact. Long-term integration accumulates drift. Commands are still published in the world frame, but the internal ground awareness has drifted along the z-axis, so the green trajectory appears to rise. The thread only mentions that the formal terrain notion will be added in the future, and no reproducible patch was provided at the time.
translations.applicability: Applies to the long-term integration phenomenon in the OCS2 legged robot dummy simulation; different simulators, contact models, or new terrain formulations require rechecking.
translations.credibility.rationale: No reproducible reproduction record has been formed.
translations.details.attempts.0: The original post only reported the environment, images, and videos, without providing the modified retesting steps.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Comparing the world-frame height with the internal contact/ground reference to determine whether the display is drifting relative to the world reference or if the robot dynamics itself is unstable.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Checking if the zero-velocity contact constraint accumulates drift in long-term integration, rather than attributing it to Eigen version.
translations.details.environments.0: Ubuntu 20.04, Eigen 3.3.7, OCS2 legged robot example; can complete catkin build; no OCS2 commit provided.
translations.details.limits.0: The thread explains the cause but does not validate an immediate fix, so the Issue cannot be considered closed equivalent to the problem being resolved.
translations.details.limits.1: The static figure shows the green trajectory above the robot; the video attachment failed to take frames, and the card does not describe the motion process based on the original text and the contributor's reply.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The contributor explains that the formulation for the formal world terrain is being expanded and planned to be integrated across optimization, simulation, and command side; the original thread did not publish a patch or retesting result.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why does the green target body trajectory leave the ground and drift upward after the OCS2 legged robot example runs for some time?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before long-term simulation or real-world execution, monitor the contact surface height drift relative to the world reference; do not assume the reference is consistent solely based on visual feedback of the robot still moving.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The contributor explains that the zero-velocity contact constraint accumulates drift in long-term integration; commands are still published in the world frame, but the internal ground awareness has drifted along the z-axis.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The green desired body trajectory drifts upward along the z-axis after multiple forward and backward movements.
translations.details.symptoms.1: The poster also mentions that the robot's motion still appears reasonable and correct.
translations.media_summaries.0: Original post PNG has been verified: in RViz, a green near-horizontal line is visible above the quadruped robot, and the poster uses a black hand-drawn contour to highlight the target trajectory; no height scale, time, or unit is present, supporting the symptom that the target trajectory is clearly above the robot/ground.
translations.media_summaries.1: Original post MP4 is open, but the browser playback fails to provide a reproducible video frame; the card does not describe the motion process based on the original text and the contributor's reply.
